designFindings: One command family has two paging models. `request list` takes the issuer's whole list from requests.receivables.listCurrent and the CLI cuts the page, so an unknown --after is CLI_USAGE (apps/cli/src/runtime/paging.ts:81-85). `inbox list` is paged by the backend, so a bad cursor is INVALID_INPUT reworded on `after` (apps/cli/src/commands/request/subcommands/list/execute.ts:26-47,61-71). The request.list page says INVALID_INPUT for both.

Offer ownership is hidden behind INVALID_INPUT 'service is unavailable', the same answer as for a missing Offer (packages/backend/src/requests/reads/offers.ts:26-27). The service.revise and service.deactivate pages promise ROLE_PERMISSION_DENIED for 'not the owner', but that code only comes from requireAuthority for an Organization (packages/backend/src/requests/guards.ts:33-49).

The refusal code of a contact write depends on whether a terminal is attached. Only an interactive run reads the contact first and refuses a party outside the book as CLI_USAGE (apps/cli/src/commands/contact/internal/write.ts:35-40). A script sends the write and gets the backend's INVALID_INPUT.

`contact get` for a party outside the book succeeds: it prints data null and 'No contact found.' and exits 0 (apps/cli/src/commands/contact/subcommands/get/execute.ts:32,42). Not-found is reported as success.

`address --org` reaches no backend row. The SDK builds the orgTreasury instructions from the person's Organization list and hard-codes network 'base-sepolia', currency USD and a default chain 84532 (packages/sdk/src/organizations/programs.ts:107-123).

The CLI makes authority and state decisions from its own earlier reads. readOrganization lists every Organization and refuses ROLE_PERMISSION_DENIED itself before the treasury read (apps/cli/src/commands/org/internal/read.ts:180-218). `inbox pay` decides WRONG_STATE from an inbox.get read before it prepares (request/subcommands/pay/execute.ts:77-103), a check-then-act gap. `request cancel` and `inbox decline` read before every write, even from a script, only to refuse a null (request/subcommands/cancel/execute.ts:23-30, decline/execute.ts:23-30).

One thing has three names. The CLI noun is `document`, the SDK is `client.paymentDocuments` (packages/sdk/src/activity/documents.ts:86-90) and the rows are activity.documents.* (packages/protocol/src/activity/operations.ts:144-163), while the stored content belongs to the documents concept (books/as-is/shared/foundation.ts:426). The task brief itself placed these rpcs in the wrong concept.

`document render` launches, and may download, headless Chrome while the command runs (apps/cli/src/platform/documents.ts:16-37). A render failure is CLI_DEFECT with exit 2 and outcome failed (documents.ts:12-13,114), so a missing browser reads as a CLI defect.

The pages and the code disagree in places. service.create's INVALID_INPUT for quantity is never produced (CLI_USAGE at apps/cli/src/commands/service/internal/input.ts:34-36; the backend checks no quantity on create). document.render's page names `kind`, but the printed object has none (platform/documents.ts:130-137). request.list's INVALID_INPUT for --after is CLI_USAGE (paging.ts:82).

Money valuation runs on the client. client.accounts.read calls one row, retries it only on a reconnect, then values the positions in the SDK with configured rates (packages/sdk/src/accounts/balance-adapter.ts:49-83). The protocol says the server-confirmed balance event is emitted on the backend (sdk accounts/balance-programs.ts:33-35).

`request issue <email> <amount>` reads the whole Account or treasury balance only to choose the asset (apps/cli/src/commands/request/subcommands/issue/execute.ts:31-40). `contact bank add` reads the whole book, then targets.resolve and parties.accounts.requirements, before its one write (contact/subcommands/bank/subcommands/add/execute.ts:24-30, bank/internal/selection.ts:16-44, bank/subcommands/accounts/internal/input.ts:111-121).

Every operation in this area forwards a single row except inbox pay. Its SDK method client.approvals.prepare dispatches on the input's keys to a request-specific prepare (books/as-is/payments/flows.ts:945-980), so one generic method carries every payment kind's composition.
keep: Write commands require --confirm off a terminal and refuse before any session or network call. At a terminal they always show a preview and ask a default-no question, even with --confirm (apps/cli/src/commands/org/internal/write.ts:31-58).

When a write's reply is lost, the CLI names the exact read to run and never retries (apps/cli/src/commands/org/internal/write-failures.ts:43-72; apps/cli/src/commands/contact/internal/recovery.ts:19-50; request/internal/write.ts:34-52).

inbox pay pays exactly the request's frozen terms. It reads paymentTerms and refuses an id, asset or value that differs (apps/cli/src/commands/request/subcommands/pay/execute.ts:109-121). It refuses a request that is not open with WRONG_STATE and gives the command that reads its current state (:85-103). It refuses a Money invoice and points to bank transfer (:105).

The approval page is the only confirmation. With --json the CLI returns awaiting_approval, the link and the wait argv at once (apps/cli/src/commands/payment/internal/approval.ts:49-60). Otherwise: rejected is CANCELLED exit 130, expired is WRONG_STATE, the deadline is CLI_DEADLINE exit 5, unsettled is TRANSACTION_FAILED naming `payment get` (approval.ts:100-148).

Document reads never print the bytes (apps/cli/src/commands/document/subcommands/get/execute.ts:24-30). Every reply is checked against the requested hash pair (document/internal/shared.ts:20-25). export writes with flag wx and mode 0600 and refuses an existing file (export/execute.ts:22-33). render writes PDF and HTML into a fresh 0700 folder with 0600 files and removes the folder on failure (apps/cli/src/platform/documents.ts:85-129).

Bank details stay private. Output is masked to last4 (packages/protocol/src/parties/accounts-schema.ts:64-74). The details travel as Unknown and are decoded inside the backend recipe so schema errors cannot echo them (accounts-operations.ts:33-35). The request key is reusable, and --input and --request-key must agree (apps/cli/src/commands/bank/subcommands/accounts/internal/request.ts:6-19).

Offer changes are guarded by expectedRevision (packages/backend/src/requests/offers/writes.ts:118-121). Deactivating an inactive Offer changes nothing and returns it as it is (writes.ts:157). create replays by request key and refuses the same key with other terms (backend requests/errors/offers.ts:10-11).

Paging: --limit must be 1 to 100 and --after must be nonempty with no control characters, checked before any session (apps/cli/src/runtime/paging.ts:38-50). A cursor that does not advance fails CLI_DEFECT instead of looping (paging.ts:52-63, :86-92).

`request get --wait paid` reads again every 5 s until the request ends (paid, declined, cancelled, expired). Its default deadline is 3600 s, and the deadline error names the same command to resume, with --org and --email (apps/cli/src/commands/request/subcommands/get/execute.ts:14-79).

Organization access refusals become one ROLE_PERMISSION_DENIED that names the Organization and gives no more detail (apps/cli/src/commands/org/internal/read.ts:69-75; org/internal/lifecycle.ts:17-24).

Money rules: an on-chain amount is AssetAmount (asset plus decimal value, currency forbidden), and fiat is Money (currency, value, decimals, asset forbidden) (packages/protocol/src/money/schema.ts:44-63). The balance headline is null when any position has no rate, and available equals balance (packages/protocol/src/accounts/model.ts:26-40). An invoice in Money is not payable by crypto inbox pay (pay/execute.ts:105).

Deposit addresses are printed in lower case, and the personal row is typed personalSafe on base-sepolia in USD (packages/protocol/src/accounts/operations.ts:268-279; packages/sdk/src/organizations/programs.ts:119).
A contact's id is its stable PartyId, and a hidden contact stays selectable (packages/protocol/src/parties/schema.ts:55-62; apps/cli/src/commands/contact/internal/selection.ts:114-135).
result.notes:
I reviewed /home/user/capxul-next/books/as-is/operations/payments.ts and edited it in place. Nothing is committed. The lane covers 26 operations: the old area page lists 33, and 7 payment.* ones live in ../payments/operations.ts. All 26 are present, with ids from frozenText and export names operation_<id>.

How I checked it: I read every cited path:line in the old code at /home/user/factory (about 200 citations, all in range and on the right line except the documents.ts:119 one I fixed). I compared each record against the CLI execute file, the SDK method, the protocol row and the backend. The `sdk:` of every old page matches the method the lane traced. Every implementedBy matches a real row and an existing sibling export with the right id: receivables listCurrent/getCurrent, inboxes listCurrent/getCurrent/decline, offers.*, accounts.balances.read, accounts.summaries.deposit-instructions. Every one of the 26 SDK methods forwards exactly one row except client.approvals.prepare, so 25 rpcs and 1 flow is the right split.

I agree with the writer's judgment 1: document.* belongs to the activity concept, because packages/backend/src/activity/documents exists and the rows are activity.documents.*. I also agree that every `given` should be "?". Across all scenario files, the only refusals this area's commands reach are in S18, which starts from an empty devnet and saves no world, and S10.9 and S10.12. Those two are budget_exhausted overspends that the page's `when` does not describe, the same rule the payments lane applied at s10.19. Every `returns` matches what the CLI prints, typed from the protocol schemas: RequestViewSchema, mapActorRequest, mapInboxItem, FixedOfferSchema, ContactSchema, BankAccountSchema and the PaymentDocument* schemas.

Fixes I made: one wrong citation, one wrong fact about the clock read, and five comment gaps or wordings. Each is in the findings list. After the edits, `npx tsc -p books` shows only the three unresolved sibling imports (parties/contacts, parties/accounts, activity/documents).
